question: For several months, France and Europe in general have been threatened by shortages of essential products, including antibiotics and paracetamol, which poses a major risk to Europeans’ health. It is no trivial matter: this state of affairs lays bare the Commission’s inability to resolve this concerning issue.

The shortages directly affect quality of care and people’s health security and expose patients to unnecessary risks. Dependence on external supplies from third countries such as China has become too risky. We urgently need to relocate medicine production chains to our continent. What steps does the Commission intend to take to speed up the relocation of production chains to our continent?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors:Jean-Paul Garraud(ID)
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.4.2024) In its Communication ‘Addressing medicines shortages in the EU’1, the Commission proposed a comprehensive toolbox ‘to mitigate […] structural risks, notably reinforcing supply by making demand more predictable, encouraging diversification and increased manufacturing for the most critical medicines, as well as EU stockpiling if needed’.

On 12 December 2023, the Commission published the Union list of critical medicines and is conducting a thorough analysis of the supply chains for these medicines to identify potential vulnerabilities2. This work has started with a pilot, focused on 10-20 medicines, that should be completed in April 2024. On 16 January 2024, the Commission launched a call to establish the Critical Medicines Alliance.

The Alliance aims to foster collaboration between Member States, the industry and other relevant stakeholders, providing strategic planning and coordination to, inter alia, address shortages and enhance manufacturing capabilities.

At the same time, the Commission is launching a preparatory study paving the way to a possible legislative initiative for a ‘Critical Medicines Act’ to build on and complement the existing initiatives3. Furthermore, still in 2024 the Commission will issue EU guidance on procuring medicinal products, to propose procurement practices that effectively integrate supply security as an award criterion.

Finally, given the complexity of pharmaceutical supply chains, diversification is essential to reduce supply chain vulnerabilities. Through trade policy and partnerships, the Commission is committed to both opening new markets and diversifying sources of supply and attaining greater harmonisation and regulatory convergence at global level.

1 https://commission.europa.eu/system/files/2023-10/Communication_medicines_shortages_EN_0.pdf 2 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_23_6377 3 See Chapter 3 - 3. STRUCTURAL MEASURES FOR THE MID AND LONG-TERM of the Communication
